chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Aban ibn Ghutfan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'My father used to give a fatwa in the time of the Banu Umayya that whatever the falcon and the hawk kill is permissible (halal), and he would be cautious of them (the Umayyads). And I am not cautious of them, and it is forbidden (haram) whatever it kills.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Baqir rule falcon game as halal while Imam al-Sadiq ruled it as haram?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the principle of *al-taqiyya* (dissimulation) in fiqh, where Imam al-Baqir permitted the consumption of game killed by falcons (*baazi*) and hawks (*saqr*) during the Umayyad era to avoid political persecution, despite the stricter requirement of explicit invocation. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) later clarified that in the absence of such pressure, the ruling reverts to its original strictness, requiring the animal to be caught alive or have its throat cut while the hunter invokes Allah's name. This highlights the dynamic nature of Shia jurisprudence, where political context can temporarily alter the application of legal rulings.
